summary: Yutaka Yuda was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Hajime Nakamura at the University of Tokyo until 1969 and earned a doctorate from Rissho University in 1990. He held assistant professorships at Kyoritsu College of Pharmacy (1969) and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).

Sinologist and linguist Yutang Lin studied at St. John's University (~1912–1916), Harvard (~1919–1920), and the University of Leipzig (~1921–1923) under August Conrady. He held a post at Peking University from around 1923 to 1926.

Yuto Kawamura is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Kyoto University (2015–2018) and held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), the University of Oxford (attested 2019), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).

Yuzo Mizoguchi specialized in sinology and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University. He held faculty posts at Saitama University (~1967–1978), Hitotsubashi University (1978), the University of Tokyo (1981–1993), and Daito Bunka University (~1993–2002).

Yün-hua Jan was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He served as a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and as a professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).
Zack Beer is a student in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of California, Berkeley and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (both attested 2026).

Zarawar Khan is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA and PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar. Khan served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).
Zawgyi studied at the University of Rangoon (~1924–1929) under Pe Maung Tin (~1925–1929) and later studied at the University of Dublin (~1934–1936).

Zayn Kassam is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. Kassam served as professor and department chair at Pomona College (starting 1995) and held directorships at the Pacific Basin Institute and the Institute of Ismaili Studies (2023).

Zeff Bjerken specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied at UC Santa Barbara and earning a PhD from the University of Michigan (2001) under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held a post at the College of Charleston (attested 2001).
Zellig Harris was a linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1928–1934). He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1934–1979) and Columbia University (~1974–1975).
Zeng Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at ICPBS and earned a PhD from the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen.
Zenjo Inoue was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1932 to 1936 under Naoshiro Tsuji.

Zenkei Blanche Hartman was a Buddhist studies and religious practitioner who studied at the University of California (~1943–1947) and trained under Richard Baker and Mel Weitsman. She served as co-abbess of the San Francisco Zen Center from 1996 to 2002.
Zenkei Shibayama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions at Hanazono University (~1930–1974) and Otani University (~1948–1967).
Zenno Ikuno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who received an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

Zenno Ishigami was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He served as professor at Taisho University (1971, 1993), president of Shukutoku University Junior College (2002–2014), and professor at Shukutoku University (2014).

Zennosuke Tsuji was a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899), he held posts there (~1906–1938), as well as at Rissho University and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Zenryu Tsukamoto was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Bukkyo, Shukyo, and Kyoto universities. He served at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities (~1949–1961) and as director of the Kyoto National Museum (1961–1972).

Zensho Kitagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1976) and later professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Rissho University, and holds an affiliation with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
